stories.headline: UP sounds high alert in border districts after deadly Nepal floods
stories.title: UP sounds high alert in border districts after deadly Nepal floods
stories.summary: UP sounds high alert in border districts after deadly Nepal floods
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Uttar Pradesh has sounded a high alert in border districts and sent rescue teams to Nepal after deadly flash floods.
The move comes as river levels rise, Indian tourists remain missing and vulnerable villages are being warned.

The administration has sounded a high alert in Maharajganj and Kushinagar districts of Uttar Pradesh and stepped up monitoring of the Gandak and other water bodies downstream of rivers in Nepal, following devastating flash floods in the neighbouring country that have killed at least 177 people and left thousands missing.
The administration in UP, which shares its northern borders with Nepal, is focusing on river monitoring, alerting vulnerable villages and keeping relief-and-rescue teams ready.

The UP government has deployed a 32-member SDRF platoon and 22 PAC personnel to Nepal for rescue and relief operations following directions from Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, an official statement said.
Four rubber boats are available and an aluminium boat is also being sent with an additional SDRF platoon.
The relief commissioner's control room is monitoring border districts, while families of stranded UP residents can contact the 1070 helpline, it said.
The Nepal floods were triggered after an ice-rock landslide blocked a river near the country's border with China.
The floods have affected several districts and left at least 826 people missing, according to Nepal's disaster management authorities.
Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal has said nearly 300 Indian tourists are among those reported missing.
The flash floods have caused extensive damage to bridges and roads, with several major highways blocked.
In Maharajganj, District Magistrate Gaurav Singh Sogarwal and Superintendent of Police Shakti Mohan Avasthy inspected the Narayani river and adjoining areas and reviewed flood preparedness.

stories.headline: The US Air Force Bomber Fleet Has Shrunk From 500 To 140 Jets As Demand Hits Record Highs
stories.title: The US Air Force Bomber Fleet Has Shrunk From 500 To 140 Jets As Demand Hits Record Highs
stories.summary: The US Air Force has far fewer bombers than it did at the end of the Cold War, but these aircraft are being deployed more frequently around the world.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A Bomber Task Force (BTF) is a deployment of United States Air Force (USAF) bomber aircraft and supporting personnel that allows the Department of War to demonstrate its ability to command and control bomber forces anywhere in the world, on short notice if required.
The first BTF mission took place in 2018 and was undertaken by the 23rd Expeditionary Bomb Squadron.

These missions not only rapidly move heavy, lethal strike capacity to forward areas of the world on short notice, but also provide deterrence, training opportunities with partner nations, and on-call firepower unmatched by lighter aircraft.
BTFs demonstrate resolve and a willingness to use force if necessary.
At issue, however, is the fact that these deployments have continued with increasing regularity despite the USAF's bomber fleet having declined significantly since the conclusion of the Cold War.
From hundreds of bombers at the turn of the millennium to just over 100 airframes today, an increasingly small fleet is answering the ever-growing demand for BTFs around the world.
This has, in turn, led to the need for extensive modernization of the USAF's bomber fleet while the clock ticks toward the arrival of its sixth-generation bomber.
During the Cold War, the USAF's Strategic Air Command was first and foremost tasked with conducting an all-out nuclear retaliation in the event of a nuclear confrontation with the Soviet Union.

This mission required immense global infrastructure and a massive bomber fleet to ensure not only deterrence, but also the ability to conduct immediate, wide-ranging, and crippling attacks against Soviet military sites and industrial capacity.
As this nearly 45-year competition ended in 1991, the USAF maintained a fleet of more than 500 bombers.
Fast-forward 35 years, and that once-massive bomber fleet has dramatically diminished to a force of around 140 aircraft.

The reasoning was obvious and practical: the existential threat to the US and Western Europe had essentially disappeared, and there was no longer a perceived need to maintain such a large bomber force or, more broadly, such a massive military.

stories.title: AI can augment reasoning but cannot substitute judicial conscience: CJI
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday said the judiciary's governing principle is that artificial intelligence may augment judicial reasoning, but it cannot substitute judicial conscience, and that a permanent apex body has been proposed to supervise the adoption and accountability of the new technology.
